hyps.why: With edge 0 removed node 1 has no input, so a conv on 1->3 processes zeros and cannot help.
A dead node 1 makes the 1->2 conv carry no signal.
Node 2 reaches the output only via edge 5, so with edge 5 cut the edit on edge 1 is irrelevant.
Without edge 1 node 2 is fed only via the 0->1->2 path, often weak or dead, limiting the value of a conv on 2->3.
If edge 5 already holds conv3x3 the edit is a no-op, whereas from other ops it typically adds useful capacity.
Removing the direct 0->3 edge when edge 5 is absent leaves only edge 4 feeding the output, risking a near-disconnected cell.
With edge 4 absent, removing edge 3 makes the output rely solely on edge 5, sharply increasing damage.
Adding a residual skip where there was no edge helps, while replacing an existing conv with skip loses capacity.
Replacing a strong conv with parameter-free pooling on an output edge is much more harmful than filling an empty or weak edge.
If edge 2 is absent, removing edge 1 disconnects node 2 entirely, nullifying edge 5 and hurting accuracy more.
